note: BBVA Perú only: BCP's site sits behind Cloudflare, Interbank's refused the request (403) and Scotiabank Perú's card page wasn't found; the SBS's interest-rate and transparency pages sit behind Incapsula. BBVA Perú's summary sheet for its Visa and Mastercard credit cards (version September 2026), read in full: the five cards it sells, Cero BBVA, Bfree, Platinum, Signature and Black, in soles. Each carries a fixed effective annual rate (TEA, on a 360-day base) on purchases, revolving or in instalments (the Black's priced from 39.99% to 69.99%, written at the top), and 104.99% on cash; the rate is effective, so a month charges the rate that, compounded twelve times, makes it. The annual membership (none on the Cero) is waived when the card's purchases average a stated sum a month (200 soles on Bfree, 800 on Platinum, 2,000 on Signature and Black), written as twelve times that over the year; the Black's waiver for the PRIME segment isn't written. A cash withdrawal at another bank's ATM or a counter costs 4% (at least 20 soles, at most 50); the Cero's at the bank's own ATMs costs nothing and isn't written. Currency conversion costs 3% on transactions abroad in a currency other than the US dollar, written as the foreign transaction fee. The moratory interest (12.51% nominal a year on soles debt) is charged on top of the compensatory rate and isn't written as a penalty rate; the sheet's minimum payment of at least 30 soles appears only in a worked example and isn't written.
